title: Hotels with a Colosseum view: which room to book
metaDescription: Five Rome hotels that sell rooms with a Colosseum view, the exact room category to book, and the look-alike rooms that don't come with the view.
h1: Hotels with a Colosseum view, and which room to book
dek: Five hotels and guest houses around the Colosseum. For each one we list the exact room category sold with the view, and the rooms that sound similar but aren't.
teaser: From four view categories at Palazzo Manfredi to a guest house on Piazza del Colosseo.

decoder.right: Superior Double Room (with view on the Colosseum)
decoder.text: At the Mercure Roma Centro Colosseo, only the category with the view in its name comes with the Colosseum. The plain Superior Double and the Superior Twin are sold without a view named.
At Palazzo Manfredi, The Hotel Guru says the Executive Double Rooms overlook Colle Oppio and the Domus Aurea, not the Colosseum. Four other categories carry the Colosseum in the name.
Hotel Colosseum lists five room types on Travelocity, and none mentions the Colosseum. A guide says its view is from the panoramic terrace, not from the rooms.

hotels.name: Palazzo Manfredi

skip.note: The Hotel Guru says these rooms overlook Colle Oppio and the Domus Aurea, not the Colosseum.

notes: Hotels.com labels the view of every category at this hotel as a city view, so go by the name of the room.

The Grand View Junior Suite and the Grand View Penthouse Suite don't name the Colosseum. A Hotels.com photo caption shows the Junior Suite window overlooking it, and Untold Italy recommends the Penthouse Suite for the view. Ask the hotel before booking either.

hotels.name: Mercure Roma Centro Colosseo

book.room: Superior Double Room (with view on the Colosseum)
book.note: The hotel's own site sells it as “Superior double room with Colosseum view” and labels the view a historic side view.

notes: A guide to hotels near the Colosseum warns that not every room has the view, and says to ask for one.

book.room: Deluxe Double Room With Colosseum View
Deluxe Triple Room With Colosseum View
book.note: The hotel says this room looks onto both the Colosseum and the Domus Aurea.
Booking sites spell it “Coliseum”. It is the same monument.

hotels.name: Colosseo Panoramic Rooms

book.note: Expedia lists it with a city view and says only that select rooms have panoramic windows over the Colosseum and the Roman Forum. Oyster reports that three of the four rooms see the Colosseum from the side. Ask which room you will get.

skip.room: Classic Double Room, Balcony, Courtyard View

notes: No category here is sold as a Colosseum view. Oyster says rooms are assigned first come, first served, so the view is not guaranteed.

alternatives.title: No view room? Try a rooftop
alternatives.text: Hotel Capo d'Africa has a roof-level breakfast area and terrace with views of the Colosseum, according to Time Out. Time Out does not say that any of its rooms have the view.

faq.q: Which Rome hotels sell rooms with a Colosseum view?
faq.a: Of the hotels we checked in October 2026: Palazzo Manfredi, Mercure Roma Centro Colosseo, Colosseum Corner and N° 9 Colosseo sell categories with the Colosseum in the name. Colosseo Panoramic Rooms has the view in some rooms, but sells no category with it.

faq.q: Does a hotel on Via Labicana guarantee the view?
faq.a: No. The Mercure Roma Centro Colosseo is at Via Labicana 144, and only one of its categories names the Colosseum. Book the category that names the view, not the address.

faq.q: Is a “Coliseum View” room the same as a “Colosseum View” room?
faq.a: Yes. Some booking sites spell the monument “Coliseum”. N° 9 Colosseo sells its Double Room under that spelling.

faq.q: Which hotel has the most Colosseum view room types?
faq.a: Palazzo Manfredi, with four on Hotels.com: Master Colosseum View, Colosseo Suite, Grand View Colosseo Suite and Ludus Colosseum View.
